title: Amazon vs Google engineering culture anecdote
why: Anecdote about a Java rewrite forced by team tooling; mostly opinion on company culture, with little transferable technical lesson.

title: Why rocket engines are turbopumps with plumbing
why: Explains gas generator versus staged combustion cycles and why engine design is a tightly coupled optimisation problem starting from known designs.

title: Why FreeBSD's integrated OS suited high-performance servers
why: Explains FreeBSD's whole-system integration, its early kqueue work, and why it long dominated high-performance web serving before Linux caught up.

title: Proposal to restructure public schooling
why: Speculative policy proposal with no evidence; an opinion rather than an explanation a reader can learn from.

title: Political argument about US policy toward Russia
why: Political opinion with no technical substance; it argues a position rather than explaining anything.

title: Crystal language pros and cons from a practitioner
why: First-hand view: Ruby-like syntax, a typed Nil, batteries-included stdlib, weak Windows support and slow compilation.

title: How AIMA's third edition reorganized the field
why: Summarizes the shift toward partially observable, nondeterministic environments and probabilistic reasoning, and how that changed the book's structure.

title: Singapore compared to Apple's control model
why: Political analogy and cultural generalization; it makes a point of view rather than an informative explanation.

title: Essay on how Halo changed console gaming
why: Nostalgic opinion about gaming's shift in tone and multiplayer culture; no concrete lesson beyond personal taste.

title: Argument that border officers may deny entry
why: Argues a policy position about border discretion; it is a debate contribution rather than an explanation of how things work.

title: Rebuttal of claims about Roman slave contracts
why: Reply-in-context that argues with another comment's claims using unsourced assertions and analogies to modern work.

title: Why XML namespaces break people's mental models
why: Namespace prefixes lack stable identity, so XML round-tripping is unsafe; the flaw is inherent to the design, not a quick library fix.

title: Preference case for Emacs over Vim
why: Editor preference argument built on personal experience; points about Elisp are opinion-led and not a self-contained explanation.

title: Novice's first impressions of the git website
why: User-experience feedback from a casual user; useful to the site's designers but not something a technical reader learns from.

title: Why TLA+ supports reasoning across levels of abstraction
why: Explains refinement as a lattice of abstraction: a property true at a coarser level also holds at finer ones, unlike reasoning in lambda calculus.

title: Company rep defends Swiss hosting and jurisdiction
why: Vendor advocacy for its own service; lists jurisdictional measures but serves mainly to promote the product.

title: How film composers' apprenticeships actually work
why: Describes the typical path from assistant to composer: admin tasks, managing rigs, production work, orchestration, then writing.

title: Critique of a blog post replacing cron
why: Sarcastic critique of a company's rewrite; mostly rhetoric about the author's team, with little concrete scheduling insight.

title: Argument that building codes are revenue schemes
why: Political opinion about local government fees; it asserts motives and does not explain a mechanism a reader could learn.

title: Critique of Black's formatting output
why: Style preference supported by one code example; opinion on formatter aesthetics rather than an explanation of technique.

title: Teaching yourself engineering with textbooks and grad school
why: Practical guide: find standard textbooks via top university course sites, and consider a funded graduate route instead of an expensive bachelor's.

title: Show HN post for a self-hosted help desk
why: Product announcement and backstory promoting the author's software; it contains no reusable technical lesson.

title: Play counts across music apps from scrobble data
why: A raw ranking of listening data from one person's logs; interesting numbers but no explanation or general lesson.

title: Why area models underpin multiplication understanding
why: Teacher's argument that rectangle area and the (x+y)^2 picture underlie multiplication and distributive-law understanding, which many teachers lack.

title: Investor view that labels squeeze Spotify
why: Investment opinion built on industry bargaining claims; a forecast and a bet rather than something a reader can learn from.

title: Practical guide to installing and running Python correctly
why: Warns that bare 'python' is a trap, advises 64-bit installers and distro-specific sources, since many Python versions and installers coexist.

title: Rebuttal of the case for index funds
why: Argues against efficient-market and indexing views by quoting Buffett and making moral claims; a persuasive essay rather than an explanation.

title: Four applicant groups every job advert must handle
why: Frames job ads around qualified, unqualified, deluded and lying applicants, and why qualified people already in work are the hard target.

title: Personal account of leaving the games industry
why: Career anecdote about pay and hours after leaving the game industry; personal experience with limited generalizable lesson.

title: How Kademlia uses XOR distance to route lookups
why: XOR of node hashes gives a distance metric, so lookups move greedily toward the target instead of searching the whole network exhaustively.

title: Rebuttal of an article on keeping engineering talent
why: Point-by-point opinion with personal anecdotes about bureaucracy and performance reviews; argues rather than explains.

title: Personal account of deployment in Afghanistan
why: Personal memoir about travel and living conditions on bases; vivid but with no technical or transferable lesson.

title: Moderator on big-tech days and front-page policy
why: Moderation note about how the site handles big-company announcement days; a community governance statement, not a technical lesson.

title: Why low ridership makes buses worse than cars
why: Public transport needs critical mass; the average UK bus carries few passengers, so per-passenger emissions can exceed an average car.

title: Engineer's speculation on Google+ and Picasa
why: Speculative rationale for product decisions from an insider's point of view; opinion about intent rather than verifiable knowledge.

title: Personal account of a partner's serious illness
why: Personal medical and relationship story; moving to read but with no transferable technical lesson for a curious reader.

title: Early experience building a Play app in Scala
why: Notes from an old 2.0 release on Windows bugs and tooling; dated, anecdotal and mostly about setup problems.

title: Copy of an anti-IRS rant
why: Political rant that advocates grievance rather than explaining anything; no informational value for a technical reader.

title: Indie developer's Mac App Store sales experience
why: Launch anecdote with sales figures and promo codes; personal business experience with limited general lessons.

title: Interview and offer experience at startups versus big tech
why: Personal job-search anecdote about equity offers and interview processes; specific to one candidate's situation.

title: Deleted Reddit posts remain linkable to usernames
why: Archive services let anyone pull a username's deleted or removed posts, so deleting content does not remove it from public archives.

title: Opinion on cyclists running red lights
why: Argues about cyclist behavior and double standards; the physics point is a passing aside rather than a developed explanation.

title: Tinder as a hookup app rather than a match tool
why: Dismisses a research article with anecdote and opinion about dating apps; argues a view rather than explaining a mechanism.

title: Why the present always feels less innovative
why: Quotes McLuhan: environments become visible only once superseded, so recent innovation looks banal and people nostalgize earlier eras.

title: Developer advocacy for Tailwind CSS
why: Opinion piece urging readers to try Tailwind; persuasive rather than explanatory, though it describes the author's experience.

title: Reading of EU Article 13 and platform liability
why: Interpretive opinion about a draft law and its likely effects; contested argument rather than settled technical knowledge.

title: How seizing underwater mortgages via eminent domain would work
why: Explains the scheme's mechanics and why fair-compensation rules make a mortgage's market value far above the discounted seizure price.

title: Why stocks trade in microseconds but houses take weeks
why: Exchanges automate the happy path while courts remain a backstop; tokenizing property mostly needs an LLC wrapper enforced by existing law.

title: Argument on the yuan and great trading centers
why: Historical generalization used to argue a political and economic prediction; opinion supported by selective examples.

title: Personal account of growing up online with ADHD
why: Personal anecdote about internet distraction and ADHD; empathetic but offers no structured lesson a reader can apply.

title: Argument that all money rests on trust
why: Opinionated take on crypto and stablecoins; makes a broad philosophical claim with informal reasoning rather than a clear explanation.

title: Thought experiment on punishment and harm
why: Moral argument about prisons framed by a quoted thought experiment; a persuasive view rather than factual explanation.

title: Insider advice: calling beats emailing congress
why: A Senate staffer says calls and in-person town halls get attention, while petitions and emails are routinely ignored.

title: Wish for a ground-up desktop OS rebuild
why: Opinion wishing for better desktop UX and features; a complaint and a hope rather than an explanation.

title: Why raw CAD models overwhelm game engines
why: CAD models carry screw threads and circuit-board detail engines cannot render; they need heavy cleaning and simplification before real-time use.

title: Summary of Windows 11 announcements
why: Bulleted list of announced features with open questions; a news digest with little explanation or insight.

title: Where web design money is for small businesses
why: Companies under about 15 people fit Squarespace or Wix; mid-size firms and agencies with budgets are the paying niche for solo developers.

title: Defense of iOS 6 App Store ranking changes
why: Opinion arguing the App Store change is good for buyers and developers; persuasive rather than explanatory.

title: Why Bluetooth struggles outdoors through the body
why: Water in the body absorbs 2.4GHz; indoor reflections help signals route around the body, while outdoors antenna design must do the work.

title: Why the 432 Hz tuning claims don't hold up
why: 432 only looks special relative to the arbitrary second; a 2% pitch gap is trivial next to DJ pitch controls of about ±10%.

title: Frustrating attempt to rent a movie legally
why: Consumer complaint about rental services and support calls; a personal grievance rather than an explanation a reader learns from.

title: Story of an employee who automated data entry
why: Anecdote about an employee's automation and firing, followed by skepticism about its truth; a story, not a lesson.

title: Replacing comments with methods can backfire
why: Converting commented blocks into methods without tracking shared variables forced extra classes; comments were carrying context the code lacked.

title: Personal account of overwork and distress
why: Personal account of long hours and a serious personal crisis; no technical or transferable lesson for a curious reader.

title: Opinion on how Google should run Android
why: Strategic opinion comparing Android with Chromebooks; argues what Google should have done rather than explaining how things work.

title: Why student loans differ from subprime mortgages
why: Student debt cannot be discharged like real estate debt and rates are far lower than subprime ARMs, so the bubble framing fails.

title: Travel anecdote from driving in northern Pakistan
why: Personal travel story with light practical tips; enjoyable, but the lessons are anecdotal and not broadly useful.

title: Essay on Glenn Gould and being more than smart
why: Commentary on an essay about originality versus talent; the musical anecdotes illustrate a view rather than teach a technique.

title: Quoted argument about systemd adoption
why: Relays a contested debate about systemd adoption and maintainer politics; opinion-driven with no concrete technical explanation.

title: How Windows file locks really work on open files
why: Open files can often be renamed but not deleted; FILE_SHARE_DELETE changes behavior, and hard links follow the same deletion rules.

title: Objection to the phrase age-appropriate
why: Emotional objection to a term used in child development; a value-laden argument with little substantive explanation.

title: Why Magic Leap's general-purpose AR product struggled
why: Without a focused use case, teams chase fidelity everywhere; Apple Watch succeeded by picking a few use cases and expanding over time.

title: Personal reaction to viewing dark web forums
why: Emotional account of encountering disturbing content on the dark web; personal reaction with no technical lesson.

title: Criticism of LinkedIn and clipboard access
why: Angry criticism of a platform's conduct and ads; includes some OSINT remarks but is mainly a complaint.

title: Grid problems with renewables beyond the headlines
why: Highlights intermittency needing backup, losses in low-voltage last-mile distribution, and battery round-trip losses of roughly 10-20%.

title: Owner's complaints about Linux laptop hardware
why: Personal hardware complaints about fans, suspend and screens; a buyer's grievance with limited general lessons.

title: Theological justification for holding church services
why: Religious argument for in-person worship during the pandemic; a faith-based position rather than an informative explanation.

title: Proposal to cap engineers per company
why: Speculative policy idea with no evidence and an unspecified threshold; an opinion on regulating big tech.

title: Three real sources of competitive advantage
why: Secret roadmap ahead of copies, customer habits with switching costs, and recognized leadership drive supply-side and demand-side advantage.

title: Argument that traditional architecture was suppressed
why: Conspiratorial claim about architecture with cherry-picked comparisons and asserted price figures; a polemic rather than an explanation.
